newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian troops to stay with Bosnia force.
newsitem.headline: Romanian troops to stay with Bosnia force.

text.p: Romania's parliament voted on Thursday to keep a 200-strong engineering battalion in NATO's new force in Bosnia and offered the help of a major airport in the west of the country.

Senate press officer Mihai Corut said the decision backed President Emil Constantinescu's calls to increase Romania's prestige with the aim of being included in the first wave of new NATO members. Only the small nationalist Greater Romania Party voted against.
Parliament agreed that the international airport in the western city of Timisoara, near the Serbia border should be made available to NATO's new SFOR force in Bosnia.
Romania sent troops in February to repair roads and bridges as part of NATO's 60,000-strong IFOR force implementing the Dayton peace accords in Bosnia.
In January 1994, Romania became the first ex-Soviet bloc member to join NATO's Partnership for Peace cooperation programme and has since been an active participant.
